newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares end up on warrant-linked bank buys.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares end up on warrant-linked bank buys.

text.p: The Athens bourse closed 0.99 percent higher on Thursday, driven up by a late buying spree on bank shares linked to a Barings call warrant, brokers said.

"A late buying spree in bank stocks drove up the index substantially," said Yannis Kalogerakis, head of trading at ABN-AMRO Axias Securities. "It must relate to the warrants issued by Barings on a basket of six Greek banking shares."

ING Baring Financial Products (IBFP) will issue 100,000 American style call warrants on a basket of six bank stocks. The issue price is $12.50 per warrant. Sigma Securities is the Greek placement agent.
A Baring source confirmed the late bank purchases related to hedging warrant positions.
"I am awaiting to hear like everybody else the government's policy statements tonight," said Kalogerakis.
Prime Minister Costas Simitis will address parliament on his newly-elected government's economic, domestic and foreign policy plans on Thursday night.
The Athens general share index closed 0.99 percent, or 9.46 points higher at 963.14 from Wednesday's 953.68 close after opening at 954.19 points.
Turnover was higher at 7.53 billion drachmas on volume of 3.94 million shares boosted by block trades in Titan TTNr.AT, Keranis and Athens Medical.
